target_pattern: Place adjectives after the noun for objective/restrictive description; place them before (or use buen/mal/gran) when the adjective shifts meaning, adds subjective emphasis, or belongs to fixed pre-noun patterns (mucho, poco, ambos, ordinals).

cognitive_shift.english_trap: Always putting adjectives after the noun in Spanish because that was the first classroom rule.
cognitive_shift.spanish_logic: Position is a meaning signal. After the noun = objective quality. Before the noun = subjective view, emphasis, or a different sense of the same adjective (nuevo, viejo, pobre, grande/gran, mismo, bueno/buen, malo/mal).
target_pattern_formula: restrictive/objective: noun + adjective (casa grande, coche nuevo)
subjective/emphasis: adjective + noun (hermosa ciudad, deliciosa cena)
bueno/malo before masculine singular: buen medico / mal resultado
fixed pre-noun: mucho/poco/ambos + noun; primero/segundo/tercero + noun
natural_examples: Compre un nuevo coche, pero no es un coche nuevo.
Es un viejo amigo, no un amigo viejo.
Es un buen abogado, pero no un abogado bueno en lo personal.
Tenemos poco tiempo y mucho trabajo.
Vivimos en la misma calle, pero en casas diferentes.

drills: Base: Es un libro grande. -> change to great book (quality, not size).
Base: Compre un coche nuevo. -> change meaning to brand-new car.
Base: Es un viejo companero. -> change meaning to coworker who is old in age.
Base: Un hombre pobre vive aqui. -> change meaning to unfortunate man.
Base: Propusieron ideas diferentes. -> change to various ideas.
Base: Es un buen analista. -> change to morally good analyst.
Base: Es un mal director. -> change to director who is unethical as a person.
Base: Tenemos poco tiempo. -> change to mucho trabajo.
Base: Ambos clientes firmaron. -> change to both documents.
Base: Es el primer borrador. -> change to second version.
Base: Una casa antigua en el centro. -> change antiguo to mean former/old friend style with amigo.
Base: Mi unico problema es el horario. -> change to unique problem.

reverse_conceptual_expression.instructions: Write natural Spanish; choose adjective position for the intended nuance.
prompts_en: I need a different approach, not the same one.
We reviewed the same document twice.
She is a good accountant (very competent).
He is a bad technician (not skilled).
It is a unique opportunity (one of a kind).
It is my only opportunity this year.
They live in a big house (physical size).
It was a great presentation (excellent quality).
An ancient building downtown.
A former boss helped me with the reference.

common_errors.mistake: Compre un coche nuevo (meaning new to me, but brand-new intended)
common_errors.why_it_happens: Nuevo after noun is read as physically brand-new; before-noun sense is not applied.

common_errors.mistake: Es un amigo viejo (meaning longtime friend)
common_errors.why_it_happens: Viejo after noun signals age, not long-standing relationship.

common_errors.mistake: Un pobre hombre (meaning without money, but unfortunate sense intended)
common_errors.why_it_happens: Pobre before noun shifts to unfortunate/pitiable meaning.
Gran before noun signals greatness/quality, not size.

common_errors.mistake: Es un doctor bueno (meaning skilled doctor)
common_errors.why_it_happens: Bueno after noun often reads as moral goodness, not professional skill.

common_errors.mistake: Es un buen director (meaning unethical director as a person)
common_errors.why_it_happens: Buen before noun is used for skill, not personal morality.
Diferente after noun means not the same; before noun can mean various.
Mucho/poco are forced after the noun by default adjective rule.
Ordinal numbers are placed after noun like English.
Simple after noun describes style; before noun can minimize to only/mere.
